reels.caption:
Everyone has the power to build their own library. And it's simpler than you might think. Here's some advice on how you can do it.

This will only slightly be a sales pitch to convince you to buy books from my online bookshop. The truth is, you can get books for cheap from many different sources. And to get started, all you need is a single small bookshelf.

I think the tik tok trend of having 1000 books in your collection in order to qualify as a "library" is completely arbitrary. In my view, if you have a collection of 20 books you have a library. Your own library. And hypothetically, those 20 books could contain more value and substance than someone else's 1000. I say that not to offend, but simply to emphasize the point that Quality > Quantity.

1) having access to quality books is the key to building a library. That means exploring thrift stores, sifting through some dust, but really being willing to pick up things you've never heard of and read into them a little. Thats the way to discover new books and new authors. Even if 95% of a thrift store's book selection is trash, all you need is an eye for that 5%. The only way to cultivate that is by leafing through everything. But thrifting is by far and away the cheapest and most plentiful way to build a book collection. At least 50% of my library is thrifted.

2) Shop used!! Buy secondhand!! If you're lucky enough to have used bookstores in your city (so many across America have closed in the last 25 years) you've gotta shop at them! Barnes & Noble/Amazon comprise 80% of the market. If you just buy used books from mom and pop shops, not only will you save huge amounts of money, but you'll be helping to keep small businesses afloat. And in my opinion, used bookstores have better selection than Barnes. If you're looking for recommendations, booksellers can be a great resource!

3) Read widely. Devote yourself to a reading routine. Reward yourself by buying a few new books every month. It can be really fulfilling to watch your book collection organically grow. Books are sacred objects. And I think one of the most engaging things you can do for your own mind is to build a book collection.
